messages.author: 85435c7e2689700c
messages.subject: Manually setting the facet dimensions
parts:
Hi everyone

I have in the past relied heavily on a hack provided by Kohske in this
group

http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/7c5454dcc04bc7b8/87ac6a2f93ad067d?#87ac6a2f93ad067d

to manually set the relative dimensions of the rows and columns in a
facet grid. Because of the new architecture in version 0.9 this hack
no longer works. I have tried to backtrack the code related to
faceting but I have been thwarted by the internal layout_base
function. When I try to run it on some sample data to look at the
output it provides I am thrown an error; probably because I don't
understand the 'data' argument.

> ggplot2:::facet_train_layout.grid(facet_grid(.~cut), diamonds)
Error in layout_base(data, cols, drop = drop) :
At least one layer must contain all variables used for facetting

Can any of the seasoned devs explain the mechanics in setting the
facet dimensions and help my on my way with updating the hack, or
provide an updated hack that I can study (I actually would like to
understand the inner workings of ggplot2 better)

Thanks for all the help

best wishes

Thomas Pedersen

messages.author: 85435c7e2689700c
messages.subject: Re: Manually setting the facet dimensions
parts:
The concept of the hack was that upon calling facet_grid() you could
specify a height and a width argument, each a vector of length
corresponding to the number of rows and columns in the facetting.
height=c(2, 2, 1) would imply three rows with the too topmost having
the same dimensions and the bottommost being half the height of the
others (more or less equal to setting space='free' and having 2
variables in the two topmost panels and 1 in the bottommost)...

Does this makes sense?

The new version is great by the way - thanks for all the good work so
far...

best wishes

Thomas

parts:
It should be fairly easy to hack this in - you'd add a height/width
field to the facet object, and then in facet_panels.grid use those
values instead of the values from the range of the data.
